title: Dissecting racial bias in an algorithm used to manage the health of populations
supports_claim: The study found that a widely used health-management algorithm predicting cost rather than illness produced racial bias; changing the target would increase Black patients receiving additional help from 17.7% to 46.5%.
limitations: The study concerns a particular commercial algorithm and care-management context, not a conversational symptom-triage assistant or all populations.

title: External Validation of a Widely Implemented Proprietary Sepsis Prediction Model in Hospitalized Patients
publisher: JAMA Internal Medicine / National Library of Medicine
supports_claim: An external validation study reported that the Epic Sepsis Model was used at hundreds of hospitals and identified 183 of 2,552 patients with sepsis who did not receive timely antibiotics.
limitations: The study evaluates one proprietary inpatient model at a study site and does not prove clinical effects or performance of CareBridge.

title: Chatbot that offered bad advice for eating disorders taken down
supports_claim: NPR reported that NEDA took down its Tessa chatbot after it gave weight-loss advice that was harmful and unrelated to its intended eating-disorder program.
limitations: The reported mechanism and user impact are contested; the article should not be treated as a clinical trial or universal proof about all health chatbots.

title: Regulation of predictive analytics in medicine: Algorithms must meet regulatory standards of clinical benefit
supports_claim: This peer-reviewed perspective argues that predictive algorithms in medicine need evidence of clinical benefit and discusses limits of regulatory evaluation.
limitations: It is a perspective article, not a product-specific regulatory decision or validation study.

title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689: Artificial Intelligence Act
publisher: Official Journal of the European Union
supports_claim: Article 6 provides high-risk classification rules for AI systems intended as safety components of products covered by listed Union harmonisation legislation.
limitations: Applicability depends on intended purpose, product-law scope, market placement, and dates; it is not a legal opinion for CareBridge.

title: Decree No. 13/2023/ND-CP on Personal Data Protection
supports_claim: Vietnam's Government published Decree 13/2023/ND-CP on personal data protection, relevant to a product processing user-entered health-adjacent information.
limitations: This source alone does not determine every consent, health-service, processor, security, or transfer obligation for the product.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
supports_claim: NIST AI RMF describes governance, mapping, measurement, and management activities for trustworthy AI risk management.
limitations: The voluntary framework is not a certification and does not prove that a control is effective.
